headline: Growth happens at the edge of comfort, not in the center
universal_truth: Everything that grows must first be challenged
fun_facts: Trees grow stronger when exposed to wind—stress creates structural resilience
Muscles only grow when subjected to strain slightly beyond their current capacity
The brain creates new neural connections most rapidly when learning feels difficult
discussion_questions: What challenge in your past turned out to be essential for your growth?
Where are you avoiding discomfort that might be necessary for development?
How do you know when to push through difficulty versus when to rest?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Trees grown in protective biospheres—no wind, no stress—grow tall but weak. They collapse under their own weight. Trees in the wild, bent by storms, grow deep roots and strong cores. Growth, it turns out, requires resistance.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We want growth without discomfort. Learning without struggle. Change without challenge. But biology shows us something different. What does stress do that creates growth instead of damage?

options.text: It signals the body/mind to adapt and strengthen
options.response: Exactly. Challenge is information—it tells your system what to build for.

options.text: It builds character and mental toughness
options.response: That's part of it, but there's a more fundamental mechanism...

q1.title: Stress-Strengthened Trees
q1.script: In Biosphere 2, trees grew quickly but couldn't stand upright. They lacked 'stress wood'—the dense tissue that forms when wind bends them. What felt like adversity was actually architecture. The challenge was building the strength.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Stress-Strengthened Trees"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Muscle Memory
q2.script: Muscles grow through micro-tears from strain. Your body repairs them stronger than before—but only if challenged beyond current capacity. This is called progressive overload. Comfort maintains; challenge builds.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Desirable Difficulty
q3.script: Learning researchers call it 'desirable difficulty'—when learning feels hard, retention is higher. The brain builds stronger connections wrestling with material than gliding through it. Struggle is the signature of real learning.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Growth is not a gentle unfolding. It's a response to challenge. If you want to grow—really grow—you need to find the edge of your comfort zone and live there sometimes.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 21—three weeks of learning! Tomorrow, we'll discover why we see colors. Until then, consider: where might you need more challenge, not less?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Growth Edge - Find Your Challenge
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and lean into a growth-promoting challenge
growTrack.activity: Identify one area where you've been avoiding difficulty. Choose one small action that feels slightly uncomfortable but manageable—a challenging conversation, a harder workout, learning something confusing. Do it this week.
